title: 2017 年全国硕士研究生招生考试 英语（二）

sections.title: Section I　完形填空
sections.dir: Read the following text. Choose the best word(s) for each numbered blank and mark A, B, C or D on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)
sections.note: 主线：无工作的未来是“荒原”还是“解放”。6、11、13 三处转折与让步最易错。

paras.en: People have speculated for centuries about a future without work. Today is no different, with academics, writers, and activists once again 1 that technology is replacing human workers. Some imagine that the coming work-free world will be defined by 2 : A few wealthy people will own all the capital, and the masses will struggle in an impoverished wasteland.
paras.zh: 几个世纪以来，人们一直在揣想一个没有工作的未来。今天并无不同：学者、作家和活动人士又一次 1 技术正在取代人力。有些人设想，即将到来的无工作世界将以 2 为特征：少数富人将拥有全部资本，而大众将在贫困的荒原上挣扎。

paras.en: A different and not mutually exclusive 3 holds that the future will be a wasteland of a different sort, one 4 by purposelessness: Without jobs to give their lives 5 , people will simply become lazy and depressed. 6 , today's unemployed don't seem to be having a great time. One Gallup poll found that twenty percent of Americans who have been unemployed for at least a year report having depression, double the rate for 7 Americans. Also, some research suggests that the 8 for rising rates of mortality, mental-health problems, and addiction 9 poorly-educated, middle-aged people is a shortage of well-paid jobs. Perhaps this is why many 10 the agonizing dullness of a jobless future.
paras.zh: 另一种与之不同、但并非互不相容的 3 认为，未来将是另一种荒原，其 4 是漫无目的：没有工作赋予生活 5 ，人们只会变得懒惰、消沉。6 ，如今的无业者似乎过得并不开心。盖洛普一项民调发现，失业至少一年以上的美国人中有百分之二十报告患有抑郁症，是有 7 美国人的两倍。此外，一些研究表明，受教育程度不高的中年人 9 死亡率、心理健康问题和成瘾率不断上升，其 8 是好工作短缺。也许正因如此，许多人才 10 无业未来那种令人痛苦的空虚无聊。

paras.en: But it doesn't 11 follow from findings like these that a world without work would be filled with unease. Such visions are based on the 12 of being unemployed in a society built on the concept of employment. In the 13 of work, a society designed with other ends in mind could 14 strikingly different circumstances for the future of labor and leisure. Today, the 15 of work may be a bit overblown. "Many jobs are boring, degrading, unhealthy, and a waste of human potential," says John Danaher, a lecturer at the National University of Ireland in Galway.
paras.zh: 但是，从这类研究结果并不能 11 推出“没有工作的世界将充满不安”的结论。这些设想，是基于一个以就业为核心理念的社会中失业的 12 。在 13 工作的情况下，一个以其他目标为设计初衷的社会，可能在未来的劳动与休闲方面 14 出截然不同的境况。如今，工作的 15 也许被有点夸大了。爱尔兰国立大学高威分校的讲师约翰·达纳赫说：“许多工作枯燥、有辱人格、有害健康，而且浪费人的潜能。”

paras.en: These days, because leisure time is relatively 16 for most workers, people use their free time to counterbalance the intellectual and emotional 17 of their jobs. "When I come home from a hard day's work, I often feel 18 ," Danaher says, adding, "In a world in which I don't have to work, I might feel rather different" — perhaps different enough to throw himself 19 a hobby or a passion project with the intensity usually reserved for 20 matters.
paras.zh: 如今，由于大多数劳动者的闲暇时间相对 16 ，人们便用空闲时间去抵消工作带来的智力和情感上的 17 。达纳赫说：“辛苦工作一天回到家，我常常感到 18 。”他接着补充：“在一个不必工作的世界里，我的感受也许会很不一样”——不一样到足以让他一头 19 一项爱好或一个心爱项目中去，而那份专注强度，通常只有 20 事务才配得上。

items.exp: 定位首段第二句：学者、作家和活动人士又一次 ___ 技术正在取代人力。首句 speculated 与 today is no different 都指向“对失业的忧思”，能引出这种论调的只有 warning（警告）。ensuring 虽可接 that 从句，但“确保技术取代人”与全段忧虑的语气相反；boasting（吹嘘）、denying（否认）也会让“警示”这层意思落空。

定位首段第三句，冒号后的解释就是答案：A few wealthy people will own all the capital, and the masses will struggle——少数人占有全部资本、大众在贫困中挣扎，正是“财富分配不均”。instability（不稳定）指局势动荡，unreliability（不可靠）用于人或物，uncertainty（不确定）是本段讨论的“求知”话题词，都不能概括这组对比。

定位第二段第一句 A different and not mutually exclusive ___ holds that...。holds 的主语应是“看法、判断”，且与首段 Some imagine 属同一类对未来情形的揣测，故 prediction（预言）。policy（政策）、guideline（指导方针）是政府或机构的行为准则，resolution 意为“决心、决议”，都无法 holds that 引出一种对未来的推断。

定位第二段第一句 one ___ by purposelessness，one 指代上文的 wasteland，空格需与 by 搭配表示“以……为特征”，be characterized by 为固定搭配；冒号后 lazy and depressed 正是“无目的”的具体表现。divided by（被……分割）、balanced by（由……平衡）、measured by（以……衡量）都无法说明“荒原”的性质。
定位第二段第二句 Without jobs to give their lives ___。本句与上文 purposelessness 同义呼应：工作赋予生活的是“意义”，give one's life meaning 也合乎搭配。wisdom（智慧）、glory（荣耀）、freedom（自由）都只是工作可能附带的产物，无法与“漫无目的”构成正反对照。
定位第二段第三句 ___ , today's unemployed don't seem to be having a great time。上句刚推断无工作会使人懒惰消沉，本句立刻拿“如今无业者确实过得不开心”作实证，是递进确认，故 Indeed。Instead 表替代、Thus 表因果结果、Nevertheless 表转折，都与“举例证实上一句”的逻辑不合。
定位第二段第四句 double the rate for ___ Americans：比较对象是“失业至少一年的人”，对照组自然是有工作的人，故 working。下文以“好工作短缺”解释死亡率上升，也一直以“有业／无业”为轴。rich（富裕）、urban（城市）、educated（受过教育）把比较维度换成了收入、地域、学历，与“失业”的对立无关。

定位第二段第五句 the ___ for rising rates of mortality... is a shortage of well-paid jobs：for 引出被解释的现象，is 引出原因，故 explanation（解释）。requirement（必要条件）会把“好工作短缺”说成前提，compensation（补偿）与 substitute（替代物）则把它说成补救手段，三者都把因果说反了。
定位第二段第五句 addiction ___ poorly-educated, middle-aged people：空格前是“各种比率上升”，空格后是“某一群体”，表示在这一人群当中的统计范围，用 among。under 表“在……之下、受控于”，beyond 表“超出”，alongside 表“与……并列”，都不能引出统计对象。
定位第二段末句 many ___ the agonizing dullness of a jobless future。本段通篇讲无业带来的抑郁与死亡率上升，故许多人是“担忧”这种痛苦的空虚。leave behind（抛在身后）、make up（编造、弥补）、set aside（搁置）都无法带出“对未来心怀忧惧”这层情绪，也与 agonizing 的语气不合。

定位第三段第一句 But it doesn't ___ follow from findings like these that...。but 一转，作者要削弱前文的悲观推断，not necessarily 意为“未必”，正是委婉否定。statistically（从统计上看）、occasionally（偶尔）、economically（经济上）都是方式状语，无法与 follow from 组成“未必能推出”这一固定说法。

定位第三段第二句 Such visions are based on the ___ of being unemployed。such visions 回指前文那些悲观推测，它们立论的依据是“失业的坏处”，故 downsides；后半句 in a society built on the concept of employment 说明这种坏处被误当成普遍规律。chances（可能性）、benefits（好处）、principles（原则）都与“负面”相反或无关。

定位第三段第三句 In the ___ of work, a society designed with other ends in mind could...。本句假设“没有工作”的情形，与上句 being unemployed 对应，in the absence of 是固定搭配，意为“在缺乏……的情况下”。in the height of（在……顶峰）、in the face of（面对）、in the course of（在……过程中）都无法表达“无工作”这一前提。
定位第三段第三句 could ___ strikingly different circumstances。主语是“以其他目标设计的社会”，宾语是“境况”，表示“产生、带来”，故 yield。disturb（扰乱）含贬义且宾语应是秩序，restore 需以“原有状态”为前提，exclude（排除）与“带来不同境况”正相反。
定位第三段第四句 the ___ of work may be a bit overblown，紧接的引语说许多工作 boring, degrading, unhealthy，正是对“工作的好处被夸大”的论证，故 virtue（优点、美德）。model（模式）、practice（做法）不含褒贬，无法与 overblown 搭配；hardship（艰难）则与“被夸大”的评价方向相反。
定位第四段第一句 because leisure time is relatively ___ for most workers：正因为闲暇“稀缺”，人们才要抓紧用它去抵消工作的消耗，因果才成立。tricky（棘手）、lengthy（冗长）、mysterious（神秘）都无法解释“为什么要用空闲时间来补偿”，也与下句 counterbalance 的紧迫感不符。

定位第四段第一句 counterbalance the intellectual and emotional ___ of their jobs。counterbalance 的宾语应是工作造成的“负担、耗费”，demands 意为“要求、耗费”，the demands of sth 为常见搭配。standards（标准）、qualities（品质）中性，谈不上“抵消”；threats（威胁）语气过重，且与“智力与情感”搭配生硬。
定位第四段第二句 When I come home from a hard day's work, I often feel ___。上句说工作消耗智力与情感，干完一天重活只觉得“疲惫”，故选 tired；下句“不必工作时感受会大不相同”也以“现在很累”为对照。ignored（被忽视）、confused（困惑）与“劳碌一天”无关，starved（挨饿）更是无据。

定位第四段第二句 throw himself ___ a hobby or a passion project。throw oneself into 是固定搭配，意为“投身于、全身心投入”。throw off（摆脱）、throw against（朝……掷去）、throw one's weight behind（支持）都不能带“爱好”作宾语，也无法与 with the intensity 的“投入”语义衔接。

定位第四段第二句 with the intensity usually reserved for ___ matters。此处说把通常留给“专业事务”的那股专注挪用到业余爱好上，与 hobby、passion project 构成“业余—专业”的对照，故 professional。technological、educational、interpersonal 只是领域分类，无法与“爱好”形成这种反差。

sections.title: Text 1　公园跑与伦敦奥运“遗产”
sections.dir: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
sections.note: 主线：公园跑赢在“欢迎所有人”，奥运遗产输在“只要精英”。25 题问的是对政府做法的态度。

paras.en: Every Saturday morning, at 9 am, more than 50,000 runners set off to run 5km around their local park. The Parkrun phenomenon began with a dozen friends and has inspired 400 events in the UK and more abroad. Events are free, staffed by thousands of volunteers. Runners range from four years old to grandparents; their times range from Andrew Baddeley's world record 13 minutes 48 seconds up to an hour.
paras.zh: 每周六早上 9 点，五万多名跑者出发，绕着当地公园跑 5 公里。“公园跑”这一现象始于十几个朋友，如今已在英国催生 400 场活动，国外更多。活动免费，由数千名志愿者担任工作人员。跑者从四岁的孩子到祖父母辈都有；成绩则从安德鲁·巴德利 13 分 48 秒的世界纪录到一小时不等。

paras.en: Parkrun is succeeding where London's Olympic "legacy" is failing. Ten years ago on Monday, it was announced that the Games of the 30th Olympiad would be in London. Planning documents pledged that the great legacy of the Games would be to lever a nation of sport lovers away from their couches. The population would be fitter, healthier and produce more winners. It has not happened. The number of adults doing weekly sport did rise, by nearly 2 million in the run-up to 2012 - but the general population was growing faster. Worse, the numbers are now falling at an accelerating rate. The opposition claims primary school pupils doing at least two hours of sport a week have nearly halved. Obesity has risen among adults and children. Official retrospectives continue as to why London 2012 failed to "inspire a generation." The success of Parkrun offers answers.
paras.zh: 在伦敦奥运“遗产”失败的地方，“公园跑”却成功了。十年前的那个周一，官方宣布第 30 届奥运会将在伦敦举办。规划文件承诺，奥运会的伟大遗产将是把全国的运动爱好者从沙发上拉起来。国民会更强健、更健康，并涌现更多冠军。这并没有发生。每周运动的成年人数量确实上升了，到 2012 年前夕增加了近 200 万——但总人口增长得更快。更糟的是，如今这个数字正以越来越快的速度下降。反对党称，每周至少运动两小时的小学生人数已近乎减半。成人与儿童中的肥胖率都在上升。官方仍在不断反思：为什么 2012 年伦敦奥运会未能“激励一代人”？“公园跑”的成功则给出了答案。

paras.en: Parkrun is not a race but a time trial: Your only competitor is the clock. The ethos welcomes anybody. There is as much joy over a puffed-out first-timer being clapped over the line as there is about top talent shining. The Olympic bidders, by contrast, wanted to get more people doing sport and to produce more elite athletes. The dual aim was mixed up: The stress on success over taking part was intimidating for newcomers.
paras.zh: “公园跑”不是比赛，而是计时跑：你唯一的对手是时钟。它的精神是欢迎任何人。人们为一个气喘吁吁、在掌声中越过终点的初次参与者而欢喜，其程度不亚于为顶尖高手的熠熠光芒喝彩。相比之下，奥运会的申办者想要让更多人参加运动，同时又要培养更多精英运动员。双重目的被混为一谈：强调“成功”甚于“参与”，令新手望而生畏。

paras.en: Indeed, there is something a little absurd in the state getting involved in the planning of such a fundamentally "grassroots" concept as community sports associations. If there is a role for government, it should really be getting involved in providing common goods — making sure there is space for playing fields and the money to pave tennis and netball courts, and encouraging the provision of all these activities in schools. But successive governments have presided over selling green spaces, squeezing money from local authorities and declining attention on sport in education. Instead of wordy, worthy strategies, future governments need to do more to provide the conditions for sport to thrive. Or at least not make them worse.
paras.zh: 的确，国家出手规划“社区体育协会”这种本质上属于“草根”的概念，多少有些荒唐。如果说政府还有角色，那真该是参与提供公共物品——确保有可供比赛的场地，有铺设网球场和无板篮球场的资金，并鼓励学校开展所有这些活动。但历届政府所做的，却是主持出售绿地、压缩地方当局的资金、减少对学校体育的重视。未来的政府需要的不是冗长而堂皇的战略，而是多做实事，为体育的兴旺提供条件；或者至少别把事情弄得更糟。

items.exp: 定位第四段第二句：政府该做的是 providing common goods——留出比赛场地、出钱铺设网球场和无板篮球场、鼓励学校开展活动，即投资公共体育设施。A 恰是作者讥为“荒唐”的政府越位；B 与 presiding over... local authorities 无关；C 把 common goods 偷换成“体育俱乐部”，范围缩窄。

items.stem: The author's attitude to what UK governments have done for sports is
items.exp: 定位第四段第三、四句：历届政府 selling green spaces, squeezing money from local authorities and declining attention on sport in education，作者还称其战略 wordy, worthy（冗长而空谈），末句更要求“至少别弄得更糟”，批评意味明确。A tolerant 与 a little absurd 的语气不合；C uncertain 与连串贬义词矛盾；D sympathetic 无据。

sections.title: Text 2　父母刷手机与孩子的“面无表情”
sections.dir: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
sections.note: 主线：父母刷手机伤的是孩子的“情感回应”。28、30 都问“研究证明了什么”，别看反。

paras.en: With so much focus on children's use of screens, it's easy for parents to forget about their own screen use. "Tech is designed to really suck you in," says Jenny Radesky in her study of digital play, "and digital products are there to promote maximal engagement. It makes it hard to disengage, and leads to a lot of bleed-over into the family routine."
paras.zh: 人们对孩子使用屏幕关注太多，父母于是很容易忘记自己也在用屏幕。珍妮·拉德斯基在她关于数字游戏的研究中说：“科技就是为了把你牢牢吸进去而设计的，数字产品的存在就是为了让人最大限度地投入。这使人难以抽身，并大量渗入家庭日常生活。”

paras.en: Radesky has studied the use of mobile phones and tablets at mealtimes by giving mother-child pairs a food-testing exercise. She found that mothers who used devices during the exercise started 20 per cent fewer verbal and 39 per cent fewer nonverbal interactions with their children. During a separate observation, she saw that phones became a source of tension in the family. Parents would be looking at their emails while the children would be making excited bids for their attention.
paras.zh: 拉德斯基研究过进餐时手机和平板的使用情况：她让一对对母子参加一项食物测试任务。她发现，任务期间使用电子设备的母亲，与孩子的言语交流少了 20%，非言语交流少了 39%。在另一次观察中，她看到手机成了家庭紧张的源头：父母在看邮件，孩子则急切地争取他们的注意。

paras.en: Infants are wired to look at parents' faces to try to understand their world, and if those faces are blank and unresponsive - as they often are when absorbed in a device — it can be extremely disconcerting for the children. Radesky cites the "still face experiment" devised by developmental psychologist Ed Tronick in the 1970s. In it, a mother is asked to interact with her child in a normal way before putting on a blank expression and not giving them any visual social feedback: The child becomes increasingly distressed as she tries to capture her mother's attention. "Parents don't have to be exquisitely present at all times, but there needs to be a balance and parents need to be responsive and sensitive to a child's verbal or nonverbal expressions of an emotional need," says Radesky.
paras.zh: 婴儿天生会看父母的脸来理解自己的世界；如果那张脸面无表情、毫无回应——沉浸在设备中时往往如此——孩子会极为不安。拉德斯基引用了发展心理学家埃德·特罗尼克 20 世纪 70 年代设计的“面无表情实验”。实验中，母亲先与孩子正常互动，随后换上一副空白表情，不给孩子任何视觉上的社交反馈：孩子一边努力吸引母亲的注意，一边越来越痛苦。拉德斯基说：“父母不必时时刻刻都无微不至，但需要有一种平衡，需要对孩子的言语或非言语的情感需求作出回应、保持敏感。”

paras.en: On the other hand, Tronick himself is concerned that the worries about kids' use of screens are born out of an "oppressive ideology that demands that parents should always be interacting" with their children: "It's based on a somewhat fantasised, very white, very upper-middle-class ideology that says if you're failing to expose your child to 30,000 words you are neglecting them." Tronick believes that just because a child isn't learning from the screen doesn't mean there's no value to it — particularly if it gives parents time to have a shower, do housework or simply have a break from their child. Parents, he says, can get a lot out of using their devices to speak to a friend or get some work out of the way. This can make them feel happier, which lets them be more available to their child the rest of the time.
paras.zh: 另一方面，特罗尼克本人担心，对孩子使用屏幕的种种忧虑，源自一种“要求父母必须时刻与孩子互动的压制性意识形态”：“它建立在一种颇有幻想色彩、非常白人化、非常中上阶层的观念之上：如果你没让孩子接触到三万个词，你就是在忽视他。”特罗尼克认为，孩子没有从屏幕上学到东西，并不意味着屏幕毫无价值——尤其当它能给父母时间去洗个澡、做点家务，或者干脆从孩子身边歇一会儿。他说，父母用设备与朋友聊几句、把一些工作处理掉，也能收获很多。这会让他们心情更好，从而在其余时间里更能陪伴孩子。

items.stem: According to Jenny Radesky, digital products are designed to
items.exp: 定位首段第二句：Tech is designed to really suck you in... digital products are there to promote maximal engagement——设计意图就是“把人吸进去、让人最大限度投入”，即吸引使用者注意力。A 把 bleed-over into the family routine（渗入家庭日常）读成“简化日常事务”；C 与“难以抽身”相反；D 文中未提。

items.stem: Radesky's food-testing exercise shows that mothers' use of devices
items.exp: 定位第二段第二句：使用设备的母亲与孩子言语交流减少 20%、非言语交流减少 39%，直接说明“母子交流减少”。A 的 appetite 由 food-testing 字面臆造，实验测的是互动而非食欲；B 把“孩子争取注意”说成“设备分散孩子注意”；C 是对“少 20% 交流”的过度推断，文中未谈语言发育。

items.stem: Radesky cites the "still face experiment" to show that
opts: it is easy for children to get used to blank expressions
verbal expressions are unnecessary for emotional exchange
children are insensitive to changes in their parents' mood
parents need to respond to children's emotional needs
items.exp: 定位第三段：母亲面无表情时孩子 increasingly distressed，紧接着拉德斯基总结 parents need to be responsive and sensitive to a child's... expressions of an emotional need——引实验正是为了证明父母须及时回应孩子的情感需求。A、C 与“孩子越来越痛苦”完全相反；B 把“非言语同样重要”曲解为“言语不必要”，且与末句并列关系矛盾。

items.stem: The oppressive ideology mentioned by Tronick requires parents to
opts: protect kids from exposure to wild fantasies
teach their kids at least 30,000 words a year
ensure constant interaction with their children
remain concerned about kids' use of screens
items.exp: 定位第四段第一句：an oppressive ideology that demands that parents should always be interacting with their children，always interacting 即“持续不断地互动”。A 把 fantasized（这种意识形态带有幻想色彩）误当成“狂乱幻想”；B 把 expose your child to 30,000 words 改成“每年教三万个词”；D 是这种意识形态造成的后果，不是它要求父母做的事。

items.stem: According to Tronick, kids' use of screens may
opts: give their parents some free time
items.exp: 定位第四段第二句：屏幕并非没有价值，particularly if it gives parents time to have a shower, do housework or simply have a break——即给父母腾出一点空闲。B 由 get a lot out of 臆造“更有创造力”；C 与 just because a child isn't learning from the screen 相反；D 的 attentive 出自第三段“面无表情”一段，属串段干扰。

sections.title: Text 3　该不该选择间隔年
sections.dir: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
sections.note: 主线：间隔年不妨碍学业、还能省钱。31 问“不选的原因”，别答成“间隔年的好处”。

paras.en: Today, widespread social pressure to immediately go to college in conjunction with increasingly high expectations in a fast-moving world often causes students to completely overlook the possibility of taking a gap year. After all, if everyone you know is going to college in the fall, it seems silly to stay back a year, doesn't it? And after going to school for 12 years, it doesn't feel natural to spend a year doing something that isn't academic.
paras.zh: 如今，快节奏世界中对“立刻上大学”的普遍社会压力，叠加越来越高的期待，常常使学生完全忽视了休间隔年的可能。毕竟，如果你认识的人秋天都要上大学，自己却留在原地一年，显得很傻，不是吗？而且上了 12 年学之后，再花一年去做与学业无关的事，也让人觉得不自然。

paras.en: But while this may be true, it's not a good enough reason to condemn gap years. There's always a constant fear of falling behind everyone else on the socially perpetuated "race to the finish line," whether that be toward graduate school, medical school or a lucrative career. But despite common misconceptions, a gap year does not hinder the success of academic pursuits - in fact, it probably enhances it.
paras.zh: 然而，就算这话不假，也不足以成为谴责间隔年的理由。在这场被社会不断延续的“奔向终点线”的竞赛中——无论目标是研究生院、医学院还是一份赚钱的职业——人们总是害怕落在别人后面。但尽管存在种种常见误解，间隔年并不会妨碍学业的成功——事实上，它很可能还有促进作用。

paras.en: Studies from the United States and Australia show that students who take a gap year are generally better prepared for and perform better in college than those who do not. Rather than pulling students back, a gap year pushes them ahead by preparing them for independence, new responsibilities and environmental changes — all things that first-year students often struggle with the most. Gap year experiences can lessen the blow when it comes to adjusting to college and being thrown into a brand new environment, making it easier to focus on academics and activities rather than acclimation blunders.
paras.zh: 美国与澳大利亚的研究表明，休过间隔年的学生通常比没有休过的学生准备得更充分，在大学里表现也更好。间隔年不是把学生往后拉，而是通过让他们为独立、新的责任和环境变化做好准备来把他们往前推——而这些恰恰是一年级新生最难应付的事。在适应大学生活、被骤然抛入全新环境时，间隔年的经历能减轻冲击，使人更容易专注于学业与活动，而不至于在适应过程中频频出错。

paras.en: If you're not convinced of the inherent value in taking a year off to explore interests, then consider its financial impact on future academic choices. According to the National Center for Education Statistics, nearly 80 percent of college students end up changing their majors at least once. This isn't surprising, considering the basic mandatory high school curriculum leaves students with a poor understanding of the vast academic possibilities that await them in college. Many students find themselves listing one major on their college applications, but switching to another after taking college classes. It's not necessarily a bad thing, but depending on the school, it can be costly to make up credits after switching too late in the game. At Boston College, for example, you would have to complete an extra year were you to switch to the nursing school from another department. Taking a gap year to figure things out initially can help prevent stress and save money later on.
paras.zh: 如果你还不相信休学一年去探索兴趣有其内在价值，那就想想它对未来学业选择的经济影响。据美国国家教育统计中心的数据，近 80% 的大学生最终至少换过一次专业。这并不奇怪，因为高中那套必修课程让学生对大学里等待他们的广阔学术可能性知之甚少。许多学生发现自己申请时填了一个专业，上过大学课程后却转到了另一个专业。这未必是坏事，但视学校而定，转专业转得太晚，补齐学分可能代价高昂。以波士顿学院为例，你若想从其他院系转到护理学院，就得多读一年。先花一个间隔年把方向弄清楚，有助于避免压力，日后也能省钱。

items.stem: One of the reasons for high-school graduates not taking a gap year is that
opts: they have a lot of fun to expect in college
it feels strange to do differently from others
it seems worthless to take off-campus courses
items.exp: 定位首段第二句：if everyone you know is going to college in the fall, it seems silly to stay back a year——周围人都升学、自己停一年显得“傻”，即与众人不同令人不安。A 的 academically misleading 文中无据，原文只说“不像学业”；B 把“社会压力”读成“贪玩”；D 的 off-campus courses 是凭空添加的概念。

items.stem: Studies from the US and Australia imply that taking a gap year helps
items.exp: 定位第三段第三句：间隔年经历能 lessen the blow（减轻冲击），针对的正是 all things that first-year students often struggle with 以及 adjusting to college 的压力，故“缓解新生压力”。A 与“更现实”无关；B“选职业的风险”是对 lucrative career 的延伸；C 的“经济负担”出自第四段，且原文说的是“日后省钱”。

items.stem: The word "acclimation" (Para. 3) is closest in meaning to
items.exp: 定位第三段末句：rather than acclimation blunders 与前文 adjusting to college and being thrown into a brand new environment 并列，指的正是“适应”新环境，故 acclimation 即 adaptation。B application（申请）与第四段 college applications 混淆；C motivation（动机）、D competition（竞争）都无法解释“适应不当而犯错”。

items.stem: A gap year may save money for students by helping them
items.exp: 定位第四段：近 80% 的大学生至少换过一次专业，转得太晚会因补学分而 costly，甚至多读一年（波士顿学院的例子），故用间隔年先 figure things out、选定合适的专业才能省钱。A 的“避免学业失败”、B 的“长期目标”文中未提；C 恰是“多花钱”的原因，方向相反。

items.stem: The most suitable title for this text would be
opts: In Favor of the Gap Year
The ABCs of the Gap Year
items.exp: 全文先摆出“不敢休间隔年”的从众心理，再以美澳研究与统计论证间隔年不妨碍、反而助力学业，最后算经济账，通篇都在为间隔年辩护，故 In Favor of the Gap Year。B 的“入门常识”只覆盖局部，C 的“再度流行”文中无据，D 的“两难”与作者鲜明的支持立场相反。

sections.title: Text 4　山火治理与联邦支出
sections.dir: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
sections.note: 主线：山火已成全国财政问题，治火先要改“完全控制”的观念。39 题问“因”不问“果”。

paras.en: Though often viewed as a problem for western states, the growing frequency of wildfires is a national concern because of its impact on federal tax dollars, says Professor Max Moritz, a specialist in fire ecology and management.
paras.zh: 马克斯·莫里茨教授是火灾生态与管理方面的专家。他说，尽管山火常被视为西部各州的问题，但其日益频繁正成为全国性的关切，因为它影响到联邦税款的使用。

paras.en: In 2015, the US Forest Service for the first time spent more than half of its $5.5 billion annual budget fighting fires - nearly double the percentage it spent on such efforts 20 years ago. In effect, fewer federal funds today are going towards the agency's other work - such as forest conservation, watershed and cultural resources management, and infrastructure upkeep — that affect the lives of all Americans.
paras.zh: 2015 年，美国林务局首次把 55 亿美元年度预算的一半以上用于扑救山火——几乎是 20 年前同类支出比例的两倍。结果是，如今用于该机构其他工作的联邦资金减少了——比如森林保护、流域与文化资源管理、基础设施维护——而这些工作影响着所有美国人的生活。

paras.en: Another nationwide concern is whether public funds from other agencies are going into construction in fire-prone districts. As Moritz puts it, how often are federal dollars building homes that are likely to be lost to a wildfire?
paras.zh: 另一个全国性的关切是：其他机构的公共资金是否正流入易发火灾地区的建设。用莫里茨的话说，联邦资金有多经常被用来建造那些很可能毁于山火的住宅？

paras.en: "It's already a huge problem from a public expenditure perspective for the whole country," he says. "We need to take a magnifying glass to that. Like, 'Wait a minute, is this OK?' Do we want instead to redirect those funds to concentrate on lower-hazard parts of the landscape?"
paras.zh: 他说：“从公共支出的角度看，这对整个国家来说已经是个大问题。我们得拿放大镜好好看看这件事。比如问一句：‘等一下，这样行吗？’我们是不是反过来该把这些资金改投到地景中风险较低的地带？”

paras.en: Such a view would require a corresponding shift in the way US society today views fire, researchers say.
paras.zh: 研究人员说，这样的观点将要求当今美国社会看待火灾的方式作出相应转变。

paras.en: For one thing, conversations about wildfires need to be more inclusive. Over the past decade, the focus has been on climate change — how the warming of the Earth from greenhouse gases is leading to conditions that worsen fires.
paras.zh: 首先，关于山火的讨论需要更具包容性。过去十年，焦点一直放在气候变化上——温室气体使地球变暖，进而造成令火灾愈演愈烈的条件。

paras.en: While climate is a key element, Moritz says, it shouldn't come at the expense of the rest of the equation.
paras.zh: 莫里茨说，气候固然是关键因素，但不该以牺牲这个“等式”中其余因素为代价。

paras.en: "The human systems and the landscapes we live on are linked, and the interactions go both ways," he says. Failing to recognize that, he notes, leads to "an overly simplified view of what the solutions might be. Our perception of the problem and of what the solution is becomes very limited."
paras.zh: 他说：“人类系统与我们赖以生存的地景是相互关联的，而且这种相互作用是双向的。”他指出，认识不到这一点，就会导致“对解决方案的过度简单化看法。我们对问题本身、对何为解决方案的认识都会变得非常有限。”

paras.en: At the same time, people continue to treat fire as an event that needs to be wholly controlled and unleashed only out of necessity, says Professor Balch at the University of Colorado. But acknowledging fire's inevitable presence in human life is an attitude crucial to developing the laws, policies, and practices that make it as safe as possible, she says.
paras.zh: 科罗拉多大学的鲍尔奇教授说，与此同时，人们仍把火视为需要完全控制的事件，只在万不得已时才任其释放。但她认为，承认火在人类生活中不可避免地存在，这种态度对于制定尽可能安全的法规、政策和做法至关重要。

paras.en: "We've disconnected ourselves from living with fire," Balch says. "It is really important to understand and try and tease out what is the human connection with fire today."
paras.zh: 鲍尔奇说：“我们已经把自己与‘与火共处’割裂开来。真正重要的是去理解并努力厘清：今天人类与火之间究竟是怎样一种关联。”

items.stem: More frequent wildfires have become a national concern because in 2015 they
opts: consumed a record-high percentage of budget
severely damaged the ecology of western states
caused a huge rise of infrastructure expenditure
items.exp: 定位第二段第一句：2015 年林务局首次把 55 亿美元年度预算的一半以上用于灭火，几乎是 20 年前同类支出比例的两倍——即“花掉了创纪录比例的预算”。A 的 unprecedented efforts 无据；C 把“西部州的问题”错置为“生态受损”，且题目问的是影响联邦税款；D 把“基础设施维护经费被挤占”说反成“支出大增”。

items.stem: Moritz calls for the use of "a magnifying glass" to
opts: raise more funds for fire-prone areas
avoid the redirection of federal money
find wildfire-free parts of the landscape
guarantee safer spending of public funds
items.exp: 定位第四段：从公共支出角度看这是大问题，需“拿放大镜”细究——把钱花在易着火区建房是否妥当、是否该改投低风险地带，核心是让公款花得更稳妥。A 的“筹资”偏离；B 与“作者主张改投”相反；C 把 lower-hazard parts 说成 wildfire-free，程度失真。

items.stem: While admitting that climate is a key element, Moritz notes that
opts: public debates have not settled yet
other factors should not be overlooked
a shift in the view of fire has taken place
items.exp: 定位第七段：it shouldn't come at the expense of the rest of the equation——不能以牺牲“等式”中其余因素为代价，即其他因素不应被忽视；第六段也批评过去十年只谈气候。A 由“讨论未定”臆造；B 与“火灾愈演愈烈”相反；D 把第五段“应当转变”读成“已经转变”。

items.stem: The overly simplified view Moritz mentions is a result of failing to
opts: discover the fundamental makeup of nature
explore the mechanism of the human systems
maximize the role of landscape in human life
understand the interrelations of man and nature
items.exp: 定位第八段：The human systems and the landscapes we live on are linked, and the interactions go both ways；Failing to recognize that 才导致 overly simplified view——没认识到的正是“人与自然的相互关联”。A、B 各只取“自然”或“人类系统”一端；C 把双向互动压缩为“地景对人的作用”，同样片面。

items.stem: Professor Balch points out that fire is something man should
items.exp: 定位第九、十段：鲍尔奇说承认 fire's inevitable presence 是制定法规政策的关键，又批评 We've disconnected ourselves from living with fire——即人应学会与火共处、与之妥协。A 的“消灭”与 D 的“远离”正是她所批评的“完全控制”心态；C 的“付出代价”是望文生义。

sections.title: Section II Part B　多项对应（人物与观点匹配）
sections.dir: Read the following text and match each of the numbered items in the left column to its corresponding information in the right column. There are two extra choices in the right column. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)
sections.note: 人物观点匹配：先圈人名，再找他引语里的“动作词”。C、D 是把话说给错的人听的干扰项。
subs: says that he switched to electrical engineering because he loves working with tools.
points out that there are enough people to fill the jobs that don't need much skill.
points out that the US doesn't manufacture anything anymore.
believes that it is important to keep a close eye on the age of his workers.
says that for factory owners, workers are harder to find because of stiff competition.
points out that a work/life balance can attract young people into manufacturing.
says that the manufacturing recession is to blame for the lay-off of the young people's parents.
sections.intro:
The decline in American manufacturing is a common refrain, particularly from Donald Trump. "We don't make anything anymore," he told Fox News, while defending his own made-in-Mexico clothing line.

Without question, manufacturing has taken a significant hit during recent decades, and further trade deals raise questions about whether new shocks could hit manufacturing.

But there is also a different way to look at the data.

Across the country, factory owners are now grappling with a new challenge: Instead of having too many workers, they may end up with too few. Despite trade competition and outsourcing, American manufacturing still needs to replace tens of thousands of retiring boomers every year. Millennials may not be that interested in taking their place. Other industries are recruiting them with similar or better pay. For factory owners, it all adds up to stiff competition for workers — and upward pressure on wages. "They're harder to find and they have job offers," says Jay Dunwell, president of Wolverine Coil Spring, a family-owned firm, "They may be coming [into the workforce], but they've been plucked by other industries that are also doing as well as manufacturing." Mr. Dunwell has begun bringing high school juniors to the factory so they can get exposed to its culture.

At RoMan Manufacturing, a maker of electrical transformers and welding equipment that his father cofounded in 1980, Robert Roth keeps a close eye on the age of his nearly 200 workers. Five are retiring this year. Mr. Roth has three community-college students enrolled in a work-placement program, with a starting wage of $13 an hour that rises to $17 after two years.

At a worktable inside the transformer plant, young Jason Stenquist looks flustered by the copper coils he's trying to assemble and the arrival of two visitors. It's his first week on the job. Asked about his choice of career, he says at high school he considered medical school before switching to electrical engineering. "I love working with tools. I love creating," he says.

But to win over these young workers, manufacturers have to clear another major hurdle: parents, who lived through the worst US economic downturn since the Great Depression, telling them to avoid the factory. Millennials "remember their father and mother both were laid off. They blame it on the manufacturing recession," says Birgit Klohs, chief executive of The Right Place, a business development agency for western Michigan.

These concerns aren't misplaced: Employment in manufacturing has fallen from 17 million in 1970 to 12 million in 2015. When the recovery began, worker shortages first appeared in the high-skilled trades. Now shortages are appearing at the mid-skill levels.

"The gap is between the jobs that take no skills and those that require a lot of skill," says Rob Spohr, a business professor at Montcalm Community College. "There're enough people to fill the jobs at McDonalds and other places where you don't need to have much skill. It's that gap in between, and that's where the problem is."

Julie Parks of Grand Rapids Community College points to another key to luring Millennials into manufacturing: a work/life balance. While their parents were content to work long hours, young people value flexibility. "Overtime is not attractive to this generation. They really want to live their lives," she says.

blocks.exp: 定位第五段：邓维尔说 They're harder to find and they have job offers，并解释年轻人被 other industries... that are also doing as well as manufacturing 抢走——工人难找源于激烈竞争，与 E 逐词对应。C 是他与工人们反驳的那句特朗普式判断，方向相反。
定位第七段：斯坦奎斯特说高中时先考虑医学院，后来 switching to electrical engineering，理由是 I love working with tools——与 A 完全对应。D 的“关注员工年龄”是老板罗伯特·罗斯的做法，属张冠李戴。
定位第八段：克洛斯说千禧一代 remember their father and mother both were laid off，且 They blame it on the manufacturing recession——把父母失业归咎于制造业衰退，正是 G。B 的“人手足够填补低技能岗位”出自 Rob Spohr，是另一段的观点。
定位第九段：斯波尔说 There're enough people to fill the jobs at McDonalds and other places where you don't need to have much skill，问题出在中间那段技能缺口，与 B 同义。E 的“工人难找”是全文另一层意思，恰与本句“低技能岗位人满为患”形成对照。
定位第十段：帕克斯指出吸引年轻人进制造业的另一关键是 a work/life balance，年轻人重视 flexibility、不愿加班——与 F 对应。A 的“改用电气工程”属斯坦奎斯特，注意人名错位。

sections.title: Section III　翻译
sections.dir: Translate the following text into Chinese. Write your translation on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
sections.note: 难点：creative personalities 是“有创造力的人”；末句 dream 要译出“我配不上时尚”的口吻。

paras.en: My dream has always been to work somewhere in an area between fashion and publishing. Two years before graduating from secondary school, I took a sewing and design course thinking that I would move on to a fashion design course. However, during that course I realized I was not good enough in this area to compete with other creative personalities in the future, so I decided that it was not the right path for me. Before applying for university I told everyone that I would study journalism, because writing was, and still is, one of my favourite activities. But, to be honest, I said it, because I thought that fashion and me together was just a dream — I knew that no one could imagine me in the fashion industry at all! So I decided to look for some fashion-related courses that included writing. This is when I noticed the course "Fashion Media & Promotion."
paras.zh: 我一直梦想着能在时尚与出版之间的某个领域里工作。中学毕业前两年，我选修了一门缝纫与设计课程，以为自己日后会接着读服装设计。然而，正是在那门课上，我意识到自己在这一行还不够出色，将来无法与其他有创造力的人竞争，于是我认定这条路不适合自己。申请大学之前，我告诉所有人我要学新闻，因为写作过去是、现在仍然是我最喜欢的活动之一。但说实话，我那样说，是因为我觉得“时尚”和“我”凑在一起不过是个梦——我知道根本没人能想象我进入时尚业！于是我决定去找一些包含写作的、与时尚相关的课程。就在这时，我注意到了“时尚媒体与推广”这门课。

words: 接着转向（另一阶段或课程）

sections.title: Section IV Part A　应用文（回复邀请信）
sections.dir: Suppose you are invited by Professor Williams to give a presentation about Chinese culture to a group of international students. Write a reply to 1) accept the invitation, and 2) introduce the key points of your presentation. You should write about 100 words on the ANSWER SHEET. Do not use your own name. Use "Li Ming" instead. Do not write your address. (10 points)
sections.note: 回信两件事：先谢邀并明确接受，再报三个讲题。缺“接受”或“要点”任一项即扣分。
sections.sample:
Dear Professor Williams,

Thank you very much for inviting me to speak to the international students about Chinese culture. I am glad to accept, and any afternoon next week would suit me well.

My presentation will centre on three points. First, I will introduce the traditional festivals and explain what they still mean to an ordinary Chinese family. Second, I will talk about calligraphy, with a short demonstration so that the audience can try holding a brush themselves. Finally, I will touch on table manners, which often puzzle visitors most.

I look forward to meeting your students and hearing their questions.

Yours sincerely,
Li Ming
tips: 第一段一句话解决“感谢＋接受＋时间”，别把两件事挤在一句长句里
要点必须具体到可讲的东西（节日、书法、餐桌礼仪），只写 Chinese culture is very interesting 等于没有内容
结尾一句期待与礼貌收束，署名固定 Li Ming，不写地址，也不用真实姓名

sections.title: Section IV Part B　图表作文
sections.dir: Write an essay based on the chart below. In your writing, you should 1) interpret the chart, and 2) give your comments. You should write about 150 words on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
sections.note: 折线图：博物馆 4165→4692 家，参观 6.378→7.8 亿人次。亮点是“两线同涨、缺口拉大”。
sections.sample:
The line chart shows the number of museums and museum visitors in China from 2013 to 2015. In these three years, museums increased from 4,165 to 4,692, while visitors climbed from 637.8 million to 780 million person-times, with a sharper rise in 2014.

Two features stand out. First, the two lines move upward together: more museums mean more places to go, and a growing public appetite in turn justifies building them. Second, the gap between the two lines is widening. The number of museums rose by only about 13 percent, but visitors increased by more than 22 percent. That suggests existing museums are already crowded and that supply may soon fall short of demand.

In my view, this is a pleasant problem. It reflects a society that has moved beyond material needs. What matters now is not building more halls but improving what is inside them — better exhibitions, digital guides, free access — so that the crowds keep coming back.
tips: 第一段只做读数：两条线各自的起止值，再点出增幅差异，不要一上来就评论
第二段抓“两线同涨”与“缺口拉大”两个特征，后者才是能写出深度的点
第三段给判断：这是消费升级的体现，落点在“提质”而非“多建”，一句结论收尾即可
